STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole green pear on a white square plate, photographed from directly overhead.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square plate is about 24 cm across its longest width (corner to corner is more, but the side is roughly 22 cm). Taking an effective diameter of ~23 cm, the area is about 415 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One whole green pear. There are some faint pink stains on the plate, but no other food.

STEP 4 - Area: The pear is about 125 px wide and 130 px tall. The plate is about 390 px wide, which is roughly 23 cm, so the pear is about 7.4 cm wide and 7.7 cm tall. Its footprint is about 3.14 × 3.7² ≈ 43 cm², or about 10% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: The pear is roughly an ellipsoid with a diameter of about 7.4 cm and a height of about 7.5 cm. Volume ≈ 0.52 × 7.4 × 7.4 × 7.5 ≈ 214 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A whole pear has a density of about 0.95 g/ml, which gives about 200 g. That is a bit heavy for a pear this size, so I take about 180 g, which allows for the tapered shape.

STEP 7 - Energy: Pear is about 57 kcal/100 g, so 180 g gives about 103 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A medium pear weighs about 170–180 g and has about 100 kcal, so this is plausible.
